findings.note: Reading the left pair reversed as sponge:frosting, both halves express 'interior cake substance hidden by its coating' (sponge/frosting and crumb/fondant), which a player could reasonably accept as the same concealment relation. Both halves read as: "sponge is covered/hidden by frosting (interior:coating, read right-to-left)" and "crumb is covered/hidden by fondant (interior:coating)".

Nothing in the words themselves fixes which pair is A:B versus C:D or which direction (basic->refined) is correct; I picked an order that felt natural but a different solver could easily reverse frosting/fondant or crumb/sponge, or swap the pairs entirely.

notes:
set-concealment allows a reversed cross-reading (sponge:frosting mirrors crumb:fondant) and its A/B pairing order is guessable; needs new pairs with a fixed, unambiguous direction. Other sets untouched.
- set-concealment: The two pairs can be read reversed (sponge hidden by frosting, crumb hidden by fondant) as validly as intended, and nothing fixes which term is the cover vs the hidden thing, so order is guessed rather than forced.
  Try: Replace with pairs where cover/hidden roles are lexically fixed and can't reverse, e.g. 'disguise : identity' :: 'camouflage : animal' — the cover word is unambiguously the covering item, not a same-domain cake substance.
  Or: Keep the cake theme but pick terms with a clearer directional mechanism: 'icing : cake' :: 'wrapper : candy', where each first term is unmistakably an applied layer and second an underlying whole, avoiding two abstract cake-interior nouns (crumb/sponge) that read like a shared category.
  Or: Add a distinguishing verb-based label plus reworded pairs, e.g. 'marzipan : fruitcake' :: 'chocolate shell : truffle center', where the coating vs core relationship is asymmetric by naming a whole item, not another layer term.
Do not change: set-agent-instrument, set-conversion, set-sequence — no allowlisted finding touches them.

persisted.note: Flipping the right pair to apprentice : cooling gives the same start-of-one-process : end-of-another-process relation as mixing : master, so a player could read this as a valid analogy. Both halves read as: "start-of-process (mixing) to end-of-process (master), a start:end pairing" and "when flipped to apprentice:cooling, also start-of-process to end-of-process".
Nothing forces material-first vs cake-first ordering; I guessed material:cake consistently but the reverse (wedding cake:fondant :: fruitcake:marzipan) reads equally well.
